hypothesis: Pixel-supported connected color components expose source boundary evidence more reliably than guessed material endpoints, within explicit color-versus-material limits.
reason: Changed evidence mechanism, restricted source diagnostic only. Stable color components can still share semantic classification errors.

supportingEvidence.claim: Guessed mixed-material endpoints and correspondence failed.
Fixed image-backed thresholds and seed reveal evidence before width assignment.

contraryEvidence.claim: Ink, pale blue bands and grain can contaminate or split color components; crop truncates.

unknowns: Seed eligibility and connectivity at each fixed threshold; material versus tonal boundary identity.

prediction.ifTrue: Recognizable stable broad blue core with qualified peripheral uncertainty.
prediction.ifFalse: Material connectivity changes or obvious ink leakage prevent area evidence.

test.action: One fixed four-neighbor component triplet plus boundaries, seed eligibility, count/bounds and crop-edge qualification; no morphology or tuning.
test.success: Restricted broad core evidence only, not head identity or segmentation truth.
test.failure: Color component insufficient for material separation.
